reason: The guide posts seem like a sensible first part of the stand that will contain the tile.
expectation: The posts should attach to the base to guide the tile during testing.

effect: The guide posts cannot currently be combined, so the stand may need another preparation first.
reaction: I’m surprised the posts were not the first fitting.
reason: Inspecting the base should reveal which part can be fitted first.
expectation: The base will show its currently available partners.

effect: The tether had to go on the base first; the stand is now tethered.
reaction: That explains why the guide posts were not available yet.
reason: With the safety tether in place, the guide posts may now fit the base.
expectation: The posts will attach to guide the tile during testing.

effect: The guide posts fit once the base was tethered, making a guided lift stand.
reaction: The stand’s assembly order is clearer now.
reason: The tile cradle appears to be the next part needed to hold the tile in the stand.
expectation: The cradle will attach to the stand to support the tile for testing.

effect: The tile must be fitted into its cradle before the assembly goes into the stand.
reaction: The compatibility feedback made the next assembly step clear.
reason: The cradled tile should now fit the guided stand for a tethered test.
expectation: The cradled tile will be secured in the stand.

effect: The cradled tile is now secured in the guided test stand.
reaction: The stand is coming together after the earlier assembly-order surprises.
reason: The battery pack and spring-return switch appear to be the power controls needed for a controlled test.
expectation: The battery and switch will form a switched power supply for the tile.

effect: The battery and spring-return switch now form a hold-to-lift supply for the test.
reaction: The hold-to-lift control seems appropriate for a tethered test.
reason: The tile needs the switched supply before it can be tested.
expectation: The supply will connect to the tile so it can be lifted under control.

effect: The powered tile rises within the tether and settles when the switch is released; the test weight remains to be tried.
reaction: The tether catching the rising tile is a striking demonstration of the invented lift.
reason: The test weight should help establish how much the tile can lift.
expectation: The weight will be attached for a controlled lift test.

effect: The loaded test showed that the tile can lift the test weight, though more slowly, and completed the goal; it did not establish a maximum capacity.
reaction: The slower rise made the invented lift feel more connected to the load being carried.

mostWorthwhile.text: The powered and loaded tests were the most worthwhile: the tether and switch made the demonstration controlled, and the weight changed its behavior.

leastWorthwhile.text: The failed first attempt to fit the guide posts was the least worthwhile; the required assembly order was not apparent from the board.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the tether had to be fitted before the guide posts, and that the cradle had to receive the tile before joining the stand.

arbitrary.text: The tether-first requirement initially felt arbitrary, although it established a safety measure before the lift test.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the tested tile becomes part of the flying fair; the contrast between its invented lift and the practical tethering was interesting.
